I’ve just added the builtin Paperclip tool bridge (paperclip-tools.js) and patched execute.js to import and use it when the external tool surface isn’t provided. The next logical step is to verify that the changes didn’t introduce any syntax errors, because the server will load these files at runtime. If there’s a syntax issue, the adapter will crash and the hot‑reload I plan to perform later will fail, making debugging harder.

The repository layout is under /home/lane/.paperclip/adapter-plugins. The adapter I’m modifying lives in the folder groq-paperclip-adapter-r3. After editing, I need to run a syntax check on both the modified execute.js and the new paperclip-tools.js files. Node’s --check flag will parse the files without executing them, which is exactly what I need.

Once I’ve confirmed the syntax is OK, I want to make the changes take effect without restarting the whole Paperclip server. The server supports hot‑reloading adapters via its install endpoint: POST to http://localhost:3100/api/adapters/install with a JSON body specifying the package name and that it’s a local path. To avoid conflicts with the existing r3 version, I’ll create a new versioned copy, r4. The plan is to:

1. Remove any previous r4 directory (in case a prior attempt left it behind) with rm -rf groq-paperclip-adapter-r4.
2. Copy the entire r3 directory to r4 (preserving the new files) using cp -a groq-paperclip-adapter-r3 groq-paperclip-adapter-r4.
3. POST to the install endpoint with packageName pointing to the absolute path of the new r4 folder and isLocalPath:true so the server treats it as a local adapter.

I also want a clear marker that the syntax check succeeded, so after the node --check commands I’ll echo a string like SYNTAX-OK. That way, if the command fails early, the subsequent steps won’t run, and I’ll see the failure in the output.

Putting it all together, the Bash command should:

- Change directory to the adapter‑plugins root.
- Run node --check on both target files.
- Echo SYNTAX-OK if they pass.
- Clean up any old r4 copy.
- Copy r3 to r4.
- POST to the install endpoint with the appropriate JSON payload.
- Finally echo (empty) to ensure the command ends cleanly.

All of these steps can be combined into a single Bash command line, which is exactly what the next tool call should be.

arguments.command: cd /home/lane/.paperclip/adapter-plugins && node --check groq-paperclip-adapter-r3/dist/server/execute.js && node --check groq-paperclip-adapter-r3/dist/server/paperclip-tools.js && echo SYNTAX-OK && rm -rf groq-paperclip-adapter-r4 && cp -a groq-paperclip-adapter-r3 groq-paperclip-adapter-r4 && curl -s -m60 -X POST http://localhost:3100/api/adapters/install -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"packageName":"/home/lane/.paperclip/adapter-plugins/groq-paperclip-adapter-r4","isLocalPath":true}'; echo
